input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based rights: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Customer's special termination triggers (9.3), plus a force-majeure exit in 27.3 and refund/warranty exits in 6.2, 19.4 and 20.5. A full-text search returns no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and no 9.4 exists. Because the Agreement runs for three years (8.1) and Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (8.2), the absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule, so it fails the fallback. There is no Vendor convenience right, which is favourable to us; our redline inserts a new 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (consistent with the refund mechanic already in 10.2) and confirms Vendor has none.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs three years but gives us no exit for convenience, so we have added a Customer right to terminate on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, consistent with our playbook. If helpful we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall have no further liability, early-termination charge, or penalty. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.
